title: Why a Conceptual Mind Needs Art
summary: Art as a need of a conceptual consciousness, not as a luxury added after thought is finished.

lessons.title: The mind that has the need
lessons.objective: Identify the consciousness that needs art as one that lives by concepts, not by the immediate moment alone.

exercises.prompt: On this claim, what kind of consciousness needs art?

choices.text: A consciousness that lives by concepts
A mind that never leaves the immediate moment
Only a mind that already has spare wealth
Only a mind that happens to feel artistic

feedback.note: The need is tied to a conceptual consciousness. It is not reserved for a mood or a surplus of money.

exercises.prompt: What is a concept, in the sense this unit uses?

choices.text: A unit that holds many concretes under one abstraction
A photograph of one moment
A spare-time hobby
The paint on a canvas

feedback.note: A concept reaches past one immediate percept. That reach is why this kind of mind has a special need.

exercises.prompt: Why is a mind of the immediate moment alone not the subject of this need?

choices.text: It does not have to live by wide abstractions
It cannot afford museums
It has no senses at all
It dislikes every story

feedback.note: The need follows from living by concepts. A consciousness that stayed only in the moment would not have that problem to solve.

exercises.prompt: Match each kind of awareness to what this unit says about art.

pairs.right: Not the mind this need is about

feedback.note: Art is a need because the mind works in concepts. The claim is about that kind of consciousness.

exercises.prompt: Match each item to its scale.

pairs.right: Wide enough to cover many cases
A life that must use those wide units

feedback.note: Concepts are wider than the moment. A life run by concepts is the life for which art is a need.

exercises.prompt: Complete the claim about who needs art.

feedback.note: The word that names the mind is conceptual. Wealth and idle time are not the basis of the need.

exercises.prompt: Complete the contrast.

parts.text: A concept holds many concretes under one

feedback.note: What makes the unit wide is that it is an abstraction, not a pastime.

exercises.prompt: Build the claim about who has the need.

feedback.note: The subject of the need is a conceptual consciousness. Wealth and afterward are not part of that sentence.

exercises.prompt: Build the contrast with a mind of the moment.

feedback.note: A conceptual mind cannot live on the immediate moment alone. That is the setting of the need.

lessons.title: Not a spare pleasure
lessons.objective: Reject the claim that art is a luxury a person can skip once practical needs are met.

exercises.prompt: What does this unit deny about art?

choices.text: That art is a luxury you can skip
That paintings exist
That people have senses
That anyone can choose a subject

feedback.note: The denial is about status. Art is not classed as a luxury on top of a finished practical life.

exercises.prompt: In this contrast, what is a luxury?

choices.text: An optional extra after real needs are met
A requirement of a conceptual mind
A starting fact of existence
A sense organ

feedback.note: Calling something a luxury means treating it as optional once necessities are covered. That is the label this unit refuses for art.

exercises.prompt: Someone has food, shelter, and free evenings, and says art is therefore unnecessary. What is wrong with that step?

choices.text: Practical comfort does not cancel a need of the conceptual mind
Food is not actually useful
Free evenings are immoral
Only poor people need art

feedback.note: Meeting practical needs does not retire the need that comes from living by concepts.

exercises.prompt: Match each label to the status this unit gives it.

pairs.right: A need of a conceptual consciousness
Does not replace the need for art

feedback.note: Art stays a need. Comfort and luxury are different ideas and do not erase it.

exercises.prompt: Match each remark to the verdict.

pairs.left: Art is only for people with money left over
Once you can eat, you are done with art

feedback.note: Spare money and a full table are not the test. The test is the kind of consciousness.

exercises.prompt: Complete the denial.

feedback.note: The rejected word is luxury. Comfort does not turn the need into an extra.

exercises.prompt: Complete the sentence.

parts.text: Food and shelter do not retire the

feedback.note: Practical goods meet other needs. They leave this one in place.

exercises.prompt: Build the denial.

feedback.note: The direct denial is that art is not a luxury. Optional is the same mistake in another word.

exercises.prompt: Build what you cannot honestly say.

feedback.note: Skipping art is the luxury picture. This unit says a conceptual mind cannot treat art that way.

lessons.title: Not attached later
lessons.objective: Reject the picture that thought is finished first and art is attached afterward as decoration.

exercises.prompt: Which timing does this unit reject?

choices.text: Thought is finished, and then art is added
The need belongs to a mind that thinks in concepts
The need is part of conceptual life
The need comes from the kind of consciousness

feedback.note: The error puts art after thought is finished. The claim keeps the need inside conceptual life.

exercises.prompt: What is wrong with calling art a decoration on a completed thought?

choices.text: It treats art as an add-on after the mind’s work is done
Decorations cannot have color
Thought never uses words
Art can only be made at night

feedback.note: Decoration-afterward means the thinking is already finished. That is the timing this unit refuses.

exercises.prompt: A student finishes a chain of reasoning and only then allows art, as a reward. Which idea is that?

choices.text: Art as something added after thought is finished
Art as a need of conceptual consciousness
A concept covering many concretes
The fact that humans think

feedback.note: Using art as a reward after thinking treats it as later and optional. The need is not a prize for finishing thought.

exercises.prompt: Match each picture of art to the verdict.

pairs.left: A need while a conceptual mind lives
A decoration on a completed idea

feedback.note: Finished-then-decorate is the rejected order. The need is not a later ornament.

exercises.prompt: Match each phrase to its role in this lesson.

pairs.right: Art is not tacked on at the end

feedback.note: A postscript comes after the real text. This unit says art is not that kind of ending.

exercises.prompt: Complete the rejected picture.

parts.text: Art is not added after thought is

feedback.note: Finished names the bad timing. The need is not waiting for thought to close.

exercises.prompt: Complete the correction.

parts.text: The need is not a later

feedback.note: Decoration is the add-on image. The need is not an ornament placed on thinking that is already done.

exercises.prompt: Build the rejected sequence.

feedback.note: Thought first, art afterward, is the order to refuse. Together would tell a different story.

exercises.prompt: Build the correction.

feedback.note: An add-on arrives after the main job. Art is not that kind of later piece.

lessons.title: Why the need arises
lessons.objective: Explain that a conceptual mind needs its wide abstractions in a form it can experience, which is why art is a need.

exercises.prompt: What problem of a conceptual mind does this unit put under the need for art?

choices.text: Its important abstractions are too wide to live as one immediate percept
It sometimes gets hungry
It needs a hobby after work
It wants to become famous

feedback.note: Concepts stretch past the moment. The need is a way to hold those wide abstractions in a form the mind can experience.

exercises.prompt: What does art supply, on this account of the need?

choices.text: A concrete form in which wide abstractions can be experienced
A spare pleasure after thinking stops
A substitute for food and shelter
A proof that existence exists

feedback.note: The need is for wide abstractions brought into concrete, experienceable form. It is not a cash substitute or a proof of an axiom.

exercises.prompt: Why is boredom a poor account of this need?

choices.text: The need comes from living by concepts, not from having empty hours
Conceptual minds never feel bored
Empty hours are impossible
Only books can be art

feedback.note: Empty time is not the cause. The cause is the kind of mind that must use wide abstractions.

exercises.prompt: Match each piece of the explanation.

pairs.right: What a conceptual mind has to live with
Too narrow to hold those abstractions by itself
A concrete form in which they can be experienced

feedback.note: The mind’s abstractions outrun a single percept. Art is how they are met in concrete form.

exercises.prompt: Match each proposed cause to the verdict.

pairs.right: The real source of the need

feedback.note: The source is conceptual life. Spare time and decoration miss why the need arises.

exercises.prompt: Complete the explanation.

parts.text: Art lets a conceptual mind experience wide abstractions in

feedback.note: Concrete names the form. Optional, later, and costly belong to the luxury picture, not to this explanation.

exercises.prompt: Complete the reason.

parts.text: The need arises because concepts are
a mind must still be able to experience.

feedback.note: They are abstractions, and an abstraction still has to be available to experience. That is the pressure behind the need.

exercises.prompt: Build the explanation.

feedback.note: The sentence is about form, not about a hobby or a price.

exercises.prompt: Build what art does for that mind.

feedback.note: Art is how those abstractions become something the mind can experience. Skip and after belong to the views this unit rejects.

lessons.title: The claim in one line
lessons.objective: Hold the full claim: art is a need of a conceptual consciousness, not a luxury added after thought is finished.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence is the full claim of this unit?

choices.text: Art is a need of a conceptual consciousness, not a luxury added after thought is finished
Art is a luxury added after thought is finished
Art is a mood with no connection to the mind
Art replaces food and shelter

feedback.note: Keep both halves: it is a need of a conceptual consciousness, and it is not a luxury added afterward.

exercises.prompt: Someone says only that art is not a luxury, and stops. What is missing?

choices.text: Whose need it is: a conceptual consciousness
The price of admission
The year the work was made
The style of the frame

feedback.note: Denying luxury is only half. The claim also names the mind that has the need.

exercises.prompt: A reader says: philosophy first, and art only if there is time left. Which half of the claim does that miss?

choices.text: Art is not something added after thought is finished
People do not need food
Clocks do not measure hours
Reading is impossible

feedback.note: Time left over is the afterward picture. The claim says the need is not scheduled after thought is done.

exercises.prompt: Match each half of the claim to its job.

pairs.left: A need of a conceptual consciousness
pairs.right: Names who has the need and that it is a need

pairs.left: Not added after thought is finished

feedback.note: The three pieces do different work. Dropping any one of them shortens the claim.

exercises.prompt: Match each case to the response.

pairs.left: Art is only for spare cash
A mind of concepts needs art

feedback.note: Spare cash and decorate-later are the two refusals. The positive claim is the conceptual mind’s need.
